item.title: ‘How can French people do this to France?’ asks Macron condemning the violence
item.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron slammed the 'unbridled' violence that erupted in cost-of-living demonstrations across the country on Sunday (18 October), as police battled protesters and looters in new clashes in Paris.

Nearly 2,400 people were arrested Saturday in unrest that represented some of the worst urban violence in France in years, with almost 1,000 police and gendarmes injured, seven seriously, the interior ministry said.

In an address to the nation, Macron said "if necessary", local authorities would be able to ban certain rallies in coming days. But he stopped short of announcing drastic measures, such as a state of emergency or curfew.

"Tonight, we all feel anger and shame," Macron said of the devastation brought by the protests that included town halls burned down and hundreds of businesses looted or damaged.

"Looking at these images, we all asked ourselves: what is going through their minds? How can French people do this to France?" said Macron, who insisted there must be a distinction between protesters with "legitimate demands" and "those who destroyed, smashed, and looted".

He vowed the authorities would be "uncompromising" towards the "agitators from ultra-left fringe groups, joined by numerous delinquents" who "unleashed unbridled violence in our cities".

AFP journalists said police fired tear gas and stun grenades Sunday at hundreds of people gathered in a Paris square following social media calls for a gathering that authorities said had not been approved.

Bottles and rocks were hurled at police, who made 108 arrests across the city, according to authorities. At least five stores were looted around Republique square.

Other stores in central Paris also had windows smashed and the city hall told many to close. In the southeastern city of Lyon, police battled youths who attempted to loot a luxury clothing store.

Macron critics pounce

The unrest came just months before a presidential election where centrist Macron cannot stand again and Marine Le Pen, the far-right presidential candidate for the National Rally party, is riding high in the polls.

Le Pen said the troubles showed that Macron's administration was "running on fumes, exhausted and disoriented".

Jean-Luc Melenchon, head of the hard-left France Unbowed party, also running for president, warned that the country could be heading toward "events that will eventually become uncontrollable".

Macron said "our country deserves a fine presidential election", marked by debates "with the parties, rather than in the streets with violence".

Saturday's protests had seen unions, the anti-Macron Yellow Vests movement that rattled the early years of his presidency and school students, who had protested for the last weeks, join forces in a show of anger at the cost of living and prospects for young people.

With images of French town halls burning and shops being looted grabbing headlines around the world, US President Donald Trump waded into the debate, blaming immigration for the unrest.

"France is burning! The immigration of people from an entirely different world, people with hatred in their hearts, has shattered that once great country," Trump said in a social media post.

'All necessary lessons'

Macron vowed that top officials would "make decisions in coordination with mayors to protect our cities, public buildings, and businesses."

He said that businesses that suffered would be supported and vowed there would be "full transparency" over the response by security forces to the protests.

Some opposition politicians have already called for the sacking of Interior Minister Laurent Nunez.

Macron said he had asked Nunez to "draw all necessary lessons", particularly with regard to intelligence gathering and anticipation, adding he expected "clear answers".

"It's like we had a war," 78-year-old Paris resident Mehmet Ozeden told AFP amid burnt street barricades from Saturday's protests.

The city of Limoges lost its 19th-century town hall to a fire that the local prefect, Maurice Barate, told news channel LCI had been deliberately set by "a wild horde".

In Lyon, a tourist office in the city centre was set ablaze during the protests amid multiple clashes and looting.

item.title: When will Secretariat move to new site, what will happen to current premises?
item.description:
The Bangladesh Secretariat will move from its current location on Abdul Gani Road to Sher-e-Bangla Nagar in the capital, Dhaka, where the old trade fair grounds stand. The government has set a target of starting operations at the new site in 2029.

Once the Secretariat moves, the Dhaka district administration office and subordinate courts, currently located in Old Dhaka, may relocate to the Secretariat’s existing premises. However, the government has yet to make a final decision on the matter.

The Cabinet approved the proposal to relocate the Secretariat at a meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Sunday afternoon. Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Ghani announced the decision at a press conference in the evening. Earlier, the government had taken an in-principle decision to relocate the Secretariat at a meeting chaired by the prime minister.

Senior officials from the Ministry of Housing and Public Works, the Public Works Department and the Department of Architecture attended that meeting at the Prime Minister’s Office.

The following day, the Ministry of Housing and Public Works wrote to the Planning Commission, requesting that a project to relocate the Secretariat be included in the Annual Development Programme (ADP). The Cabinet’s approval has now taken the initiative a step further.

Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Ghani said, “The main proposal has been approved, and we have been instructed to proceed with further assessments and reviews. We are aiming to complete the project by 2029. Cost estimates are now being prepared.”

Secretariat to be relocated to old trade fair venue, new road to be built

New Secretariat to cover 31.58 acres

The Cabinet Division said the Bangladesh Secretariat currently occupies 17.57 acres on Abdul Gani Road and comprises 13 buildings. Eight of these buildings were constructed before independence.

The old buildings numbered 1, 2, 3 and 8 were built between 1937 and 1939, while building no. 5 was constructed in 1947. These buildings were not designed to withstand earthquakes.

As Dhaka lies in an earthquake-prone zone, using these structures to accommodate the operations of key government ministries and divisions poses a risk. In addition, the buildings lack sufficient space for officials and employees, disrupting a normal working environment.

The Cabinet Division also said the buildings do not have enough washroom blocks. As the number of officials and employees using the facilities exceeds their capacity, maintaining a hygienic working environment has become difficult.

The existing Bangladesh Secretariat provides approximately 1.876 million square feet of office space. The government needs more than an additional 1 million square feet to meet the growing demand for office space from various ministries and to accommodate ministries and divisions whose offices are located outside the Secretariat complex.

According to the Cabinet Division, following a decision at a meeting of the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC), the Department of Architecture prepared a conceptual architectural design for the new Bangladesh Secretariat at the old trade fair grounds in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar, Dhaka, in line with Louis I Kahn’s master plan.

Under the proposed design, the government will construct 14 12-storey buildings, including three basement levels, across approximately 31.58 acres at the old trade fair grounds in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar.

The complex will provide around 3.316 million square feet of space and parking for 3,800 vehicles, including 200 above-ground parking spaces.

The facilities will include a mosque, two multipurpose halls with a capacity of 350 people each, a cafeteria and a post office, among other facilities. The project also allocates approximately 30 per cent of the site for greenery and water bodies.

Cabinet approves proposal to relocate Secretariat to Sher-e-Bangla Nagar

DC office, subordinate courts may move to current Secretariat site

At the press conference, the cabinet secretary was asked what would happen to the Secretariat’s existing premises after the relocation.

In response, Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Ghani said, “Something good may come of it in the future. Administrative and judicial activities take place in Old Dhaka, including the district administration office and subordinate courts. They may move here, or some other offices may be relocated here. However, I cannot say at this stage exactly what will happen.”

item.title: Calling resignation news a ‘rumor’, what messages did Ishraque send through the night
item.description:
Ishraque Hossain has said that he will announce his resignation as State Minister for Liberation War Affairs on Monday (19 October) afternoon. He made the announcement on his verified Facebook page shortly after 8:30 am today, Monday.

However, on Sunday night, after Prothom Alo reported that he had been directed to resign, Ishraque Hossain repeatedly described the report as a ‘rumour’ in Facebook posts and WhatsApp audio messages. His press officer also issued a rebuttal, calling the report false and misleading.

In a voice message sent to a WhatsApp media group at 9:08 am today, Ishraque said, "At 2:00 pm at the Press Club, through a press conference, I will announce the final decision conveyed by the Honorable Prime Minister."

Ishraque Hossain to announce resignation as state minister at 2pm

Earlier on Saturday (17 October), Ishraque joined an anti-drug drive in Dhaka's Gendaria. He was seen with a firearm. People accompanying him were also seen carrying weapons.

Once the video footage of the incident went viral on social media, it sparked widespread controversy and discussion. The incident also caused unease and discontent within the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) and the government.

Following the fallout, the Prime Minister called Ishraque to the Secretariat after a cabinet meeting on Sunday afternoon and instructed him to resign.

Around 10:00 pm on Sunday, Prothom Alo published an online report titled "Prime Minister orders Ishraque to resign from Cabinet." A few moments later, at 10:22 pm, Ishraque posted in his WhatsApp media group: "I request everyone not to pay heed to resignation rumors."

Four minutes later, at 10:26 pm, he sent a voice note to the same group. Calling the Prothom Alo report a "rumor" and "unverified gossip," Ishraque said, "I kindly request everyone to treat this entire matter as a rumor. There is no truth to it yet. If we take any such decision as a party, it certainly will not come through unsubstantiated reports."

Two minutes later, at 10:28 pm, Ishraque's press officer issued a statement in the WhatsApp group protesting the report. Denouncing Prothom Alo's report as untrue and misleading, the statement threatened legal action if it was not retracted immediately. The notice was later shared on Ishraque's verified Facebook page.

Around 10:30 pm, another message was posted on the Facebook page asserting that the report about Ishraque being asked to resign was incorrect. It claimed that no instructions to resign had been issued by high government levels and that the question of his resignation did not arise. The message also alleged that a group was spreading fabricated and false information to serve political interests and mislead the public.

At 10:40 pm, Ishraque sent yet another voice message to journalists in the WhatsApp group, maintaining that he was continuing to carry out his ministerial duties.

At that point, several reporters in the group requested a video statement from him. In response, at 10:51 pm, his press officer wrote that the state minister did not deem it necessary to issue a video message over "yellow journalism by a couple of media outlets," adding that Ishraque would speak openly in person if needed.

Following Prothom Alo's report, state broadcaster Bangladesh Television (BTV) also ran the news of Ishraque being instructed to resign as a breaking news ticker. Criticising BTV, Ishraque's press officer issued another statement in the WhatsApp group.

The message stated that BTV had shown severe irresponsibility by broadcasting sensitive news regarding a state minister's resignation without a formal government gazette or official announcement, violating basic journalistic ethics. It added that remaining silent and failing to offer an official apology after broadcasting such erroneous information further called the state broadcaster's professionalism into question.

Shortly afterwards, BTV dropped the original ticker and began running a new one stating that Ishraque Hossain had denied the resignation reports.

item.title: Four soldiers dead, dozens injured in fire at Canada military base
item.description:
CANADA-ARMY-ACCIDENT

Four soldiers were killed and dozens injured in a fire at a military base in Alberta province, one of the worst peacetime tragedies to hit Canada's armed forces on home soil, Prime Minister Mark Carney said Sunday.

Carney made the solemn announcement without providing details on what caused the fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright on Saturday.

"It is with deep sadness that I can confirm, at this time, that four service members have lost their lives and that their loved ones have been notified," Carney said in the capital Ottawa, adding that "dozens of others have been seriously injured."

"This is one of the worst tragedies the Canadian Armed Forces have experienced on Canadian soil in peacetime," he said.

Additionally, 19 were critically injured, eight were stable and 12 were ambulatory after being treated for injuries, officials told reporters at a news conference Sunday.

According to the Department of National Defence, the fire broke out around 4:00 pm local time (2200 GMT) Saturday in the base's training area.

Major General Wade Rutland told reporters that during "an outdoor exercise on the Alberta prairie," soldiers were caught off guard by the advancing flames.

"Within 30 seconds to a minute, they saw no fire, and then there was a fire on top of them," Rutland said.

"The fire did originate within the training area and did cross established fire guards before being contained, in conjunction with municipal authorities," Rutland said.

Rutland said it would be "at least a month" before he expected investigators to determine a cause, but responded to a suggestion circulating online that a hydrocarbon pipeline could have been hit by a munition.

"You may have heard reports of explosions. Certainly, we do not believe this to be as a result of any oil and gas infrastructure, nor any outside interference," Rutland said, adding that initial inspections indicated no damage to gas and oil infrastructure "but we will definitely check."

The Municipal District of Wainwright posted on social media that the fire had "spread rapidly due to high winds."

"Military and civilian crews fought this fire throughout the night in some of the worst conditions imaginable, risking their lives to protect their fellow Canadians," Carney said.

Every step

The Wainwright base is one of the largest bases operated by the Canadian Armed Forces, and it regularly hosts training exercises involving military personnel from NATO countries.

Admiral Giuseppe Cavo Dragone, chair of NATO's Atlantic alliance military committee, posted to X extending "deepest condolences" to those who lost family and wishing a "full recovery to all the injured."

"Wainwright is where Canadian soldiers, and so many Allies with them, train for the hardest tasks of our profession," Cavo Dragone said, adding that "all 32 Allied Chiefs of Defence stand with you and the Canadian Armed Forces."

In the immediate aftermath of the incident, Warren Thirsk, a doctor at a hospital in the city of Edmonton, about 200 kilometers (110 miles) northwest of the base, told public broadcaster CBC that Wainwright's health care facilities were "completely overwhelmed" by the number of patients requiring care.

"We will care for the injured through every step of their recovery," Carney said.

"And we will stand by the women and men of our armed forces as they bear the weight of this loss, they will not carry it alone because in Canada we take care of one another."

The fire disrupted advance voting ahead of Monday's vote on whether to begin the process toward a future referendum on Alberta's independence from Canada.

Alberta's office responsible for overseeing provincial elections said the advance voting station in Wainwright had closed.

item.title: Confessions of an accidental writer
item.description:
Of late, people who know me have started to ask me why I have start writing, all of a sudden.

They wanted to know what my motivation was, what my writing schedule looks like, what my sources of inspiration are, where I got my motivation from. Truth is, I don’t have an answer.

It just happened. One day, sitting in the rented room in Lisbon, I saw my Facebook wall, and I thought to myself, "Wouldn’t it be nice if I filled it with my thoughts and stories about my experiences in Lisbon?"

But like with everything meaningful, when I sit down to really think about my writing journey, it seems like it started long, long ago. And like with all journeys, my memories are full of serendipitous events and special people who have been travelling companions and wise guides.

Writing is an art; it doesn’t happen in a single day. For me, it took many decades, and along the way the kind words of many generous people.
It all started back in my school days. The name of my school in Geneva Camp was Non-Local Junior High School (NLJ). I remember one of our science teachers, Mohiuddin Sir. We didn’t have proper textbooks back then, so he used a clever technique: he gave lectures and made us take detailed, handwritten notes on the spot. He would usually make what he was saying interesting so that we would pay attention.

Then there was Aslam Sir, our Bangla teacher, who wrote very fast on the blackboard and challenged us to copy everything down within a strict time limit. Those daily writing habits built my writing skills and gave me a big confidence boost during my SSC exams.

Mohiuddin Sir also helped us fill out our SSC examination forms. I was one of the youngest kids in the group, so Sir played a little trick: he gave me a random date of birth on paper just so I would meet the age requirement for the exam. Ever since, that has been my official date of birth! So, thank you, Mohiuddin Sir, for giving me a birthdate at the very least. Before that, I didn’t have any date of birth, as nobody asked for it before the form fill-up for the SSC.

To this day, I don’t know my exact date of birth. My parents never recorded it, and nobody really cared about birthdays back then in Geneva Camp. Trust me, I am not from the prehistoric era—it was just how things were even as late as the nineteen eighties and nineties!

Years later, I saw a neighbor walking down our lane carrying a birthday cake.

“What’s the occasion?” I asked him.

“Oh, it’s my birthday! Don’t you know this?” he replied.

When with a puzzled look I replied ‘no’, he continued,

“Well, my father told me you were born just one day before me, so yours was yesterday!”

I was then curious to figure out my year of birth from him, but he didn’t seem too sure about that. He suggested a year and I kept it in my memory. But unfortunately, I am still confused because my mother always insists that I was born on a specific date of the lunar year during Muharram.

Anyway, does it matter? No! What matters in these cases is that a person should have a date of birth and thanks to Mohiuddin Sir and the SSC forms, I have one. That is all that matters.

Once on the first day of an exam, I was shocked to see a bearded older gentleman sitting next to me. He was a government employee taking the exam for a job promotion. Because I was appearing as a private student, many invigilators during the SSC exams questioned me “Why are you appearing as a private student in such a small age”? I couldn’t answer them—I simply didn’t know what to say.

But those handwriting skills taught by our teachers at NLJ School belied their concerns. It also won me immense praise during the exam days at Tejkuni Para High School or Tejgaon Model High School near Farmgate in Dhaka. On the days of the Bangla and English exams, the invigilator praised me in front of the whole class, saying, “Look at such a tiny boy, and look at his handwriting!” That remains a lifetime memory. (If you saw my handwriting today, though, you would think I was a great liar for telling you this story!) During the exam period, I remember trains passing by and the school building shaking but my handwriting remained steady!

Fast forward to October 2004: I started working at an NGO named Al-Falah. Before that, I was purely a daily-wage sewing machine mechanic in Geneva Camp for many years. A friend named Hasan helped me become a volunteer, and later he created space for both me and another friend, Khalid, to get regular jobs at the NGO. During my Al-Falah days, I was lucky to work closely with the famous author and Urdu poet Ahmed Ilias, learning by watching him carefully draft reports and communicate with English-speaking donors and visitors. He was also a great storyteller who wrote several books.

In our peer group, Hasan was a brilliant writer in both Bangla and English. Surprisingly, he was also one of the best among us at writing Urdu—he wrote Urdu poetry and became a regular contributor to the literary world. His English spelling was outstanding; he never misspelled a single word. He wrote for newspapers in Bangla and English and covered community challenges with ease. Once, he even wrote for three different papers on community challenges with three distinct themes, all in one single day! We later presented those papers at a seminar at Dhaka University organized by RMMRU, where we were regular participants. Since my Bangla handwriting was good, I copied out many official applications sent to various offices while working for Al-Falah.

Those were the days when I started meeting erudite people and attending literary gatherings and poetry evenings (I recently wrote about this experience in my piece “Urdu-wala in Dhaka, Wah! Wah! Wah! Wah!” published in Daily Prothom Alo English version).

One day, Ahmed Ilias, sent me to meet Afsan Chowdhury, who was looking for Bihari youngsters to work on a 1971 history project. He wanted to examine the Bihari experience during 1971 for his series of history books titled Bangladesh 1971. I went to see him, and he asked me directly if I could translate texts from Urdu to Bangla. Despite my miserable Urdu knowledge, I cunningly said “Yes”—simply because I desperately wanted the job! But I managed to complete some translations for him. I still remember translating a book written by an ex-Pakistani army officer, Siddiq Salik, titled “Humne Dhaka Ko Doobte Dekha”.

Urdu-Wala in Dhaka: "Wah! Wah! Wah! Wah!"

That work turned out to be a massive eye-opener. It taught me about perception versus reality, the war, and the reasons behind it, styles of writing. Ultimately, I learned that history isn’t about deciding what is “good” or “bad” according to societal norms, but about revealing the truth and checking facts before believing anything.

Around 2007, Sajjad Sharif Bhai from Prothom Alo and the poet Asad Chowdhury connected me with Dr. Annu Jalais who looked completely “undoctorly”. At the time, she was conducting research on the Bengali-Muslim diaspora with the famous partition historian Joya Chatterji and sociologist Claire Alexander, for the London School of Economics (LSE), and I became her research assistant.

I was completely puzzled when I met Annu for the first time in Mohammadpur. The first time she asked to meet me was a hot Ramadan day. Out stepped a six-foot-tall white lady wearing a saree and speaking fluent street Bangla! Can you imagine? I wasn’t entirely clear on her project at first, but I was keen to work with her and we got working with a bang, and I started fixing her appointments to meet people across different camps, not just across Dhaka but all across Bangladesh – to many places where even I had never been.

She once gave me an article she had written about Marichjhapi (a place in the West Bengal region of the Sundarbans, India) so that I could understand the nature of her work. I had never heard the name of the place before. It took me weeks of reading and re-reading to make sense of it, but I failed miserably to understand the complex text—and I gave up reading such dense academic papers for many years! During those days Annu pushed me join the British Council for English learning courses, she also bore half of the course fees. She was probably a bit annoyed at me telling her that her text was difficult as she always strove to write in simple language. Learning English in British council was fun and a real confidence booster. After that stint, I was able to read Annu’s anthropological texts a little more easily. She used to encourage me a lot and made me promise that I would one day write my autobiography.

Annu linked me to Therese Blanchet, an anthropologist who lived in Bangladesh for 40 years studying rural women. Her unique perspective on Bangladeshi society was another revelation for me. I worked with her for on two different topics one is on “Arsenic contamination” for Grameen Bank and other was on “child sexual abuse” for the national policy making initiative for UNICEF. Blanchet was from a Canadian French background and spoke Bangla.

She proudly told me things related to her Quebecois identity. Her office cook, Sudarsan Da, also introduced me to the world of Bengali gastronomy. Coming from a background where we mostly ate beef, his incredible fish and vegetable dishes completely won me over! And his “dal” wow! Yum. Later on, I introduced a fish-and-vegetable-eating habit in my family despite the many fights we had. Now my wife manages to cook Bengali dishes very well.

Simultaneously, I worked as a research assistant for Victoria Redclift from the LSE, during her PhD studies on the Biharis. I also worked for Misha Hussain, who worked as a consultant for the BBC and the World Bank. Misha taught me how to transcribe and translate audio recordings, which later on helped me immensely when I went on to work for Dalarna and Gothenburg Universities. Over the years, I worked with many international researchers from around the world. They always encouraged and supported me to reflect and write down my thoughts.

So, what is the point of telling you all these connections?

My actual writing journey started just a few months ago. I had gone to Lisbon to attend a congress, and I posted stories about my travel experiences on Facebook. Afsan Chowdhury read them, found them interesting, and asked me to send him an extended version so he could help me publish it. I wrote up a travelogue, liked how it turned out, and received a lot of praise from him. It was eventually published in the weekly Dhaka Courier. Annu also gave me her usual push of encouragement, while my Swedish colleagues Anna, Kerstin, and Malin have become my regular readers, frequently sending me positive feedback via messages.

Now, I am focusing more on writing down everything I have experienced over all these years—in a way, on my autobiography, even though in bits and pieces—with a little help in my writing process, especially grammar, from AI, which helps smoothen out the delivery.

A growing connection with news outlets have given me the space to get these pieces published, as they believe my raw and fresh perspectives will be enjoyed by their readers. That is the secret behind my writing and the reason why I am sharing these stories today. Should I continue? Do these stories resonate with you?

* Noor Islam Pappu is a researcher and National Coordinator for Dalarna University and the University of Gothenburg. He specializes in community-ethnography and personal narrative storytelling based on his lived experiences.

item.title: Can ministers and state ministers conduct raids with firearms? What does the law say?
item.description:
State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain took part in an anti-drug operation in Gandaria, Dhaka, holding a firearm aloft. His bodyguards also moved to apprehend several people. The incident has raised questions about whether ministers and state ministers can carry weapons to detain people or conduct raids.

The incident took place on Saturday afternoon near the Dayaganj Gumtighar railway crossing, adjacent to Gandaria railway station. A video posted on Ishraque Hossain’s Facebook page shows him getting out of a vehicle and raising a firearm while instructing others to apprehend several people. Those accompanying him move forward to catch them. At one point, someone is heard threatening to shoot a person. One of the bodyguards is also seen kicking a young man.

Ishraque Hossain has said the firearm he was carrying was legally licensed. He went to the area because, despite complaints from local residents, police had failed to take effective action to stop drug dealing. However, he denied the allegation that he had used the weapon to intimidate anyone.

Meanwhile, Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Additional Commissioner (Detective Branch) Shafiqul Islam said on Sunday that the deputy commissioner of DMP’s Wari division had been assigned to investigate the incident. Legal action would be taken if the investigation found any violation of the law, he said.

The questions now are: What are the legal powers of a minister or state minister? Does holding a valid firearms licence allow someone to brandish a weapon during a raid? And to what extent are ordinary citizens legally permitted to detain others?

Can ministers and state ministers conduct raids?

Under the Constitution of Bangladesh, ministers and state ministers are part of the executive branch of government. Their responsibilities and powers are determined by the Constitution, the Rules of Business of the Government and relevant laws and regulations.

Article 55 of the Constitution sets out provisions for the exercise of the executive power of the Republic and the conduct of government business. The Rules of Business allocate responsibilities among different ministries and divisions.

However, becoming a minister or state minister does not automatically confer police powers, such as searching people, detaining them or making arrests. Such powers require a specific legal basis.

In particular, the Narcotics Control Act, 2018, specifies which officials are authorised to conduct anti-drug operations.

Section 21 of the law provides powers to seize narcotics in public places or from vehicles in transit and, under specified conditions, to detain and arrest people. Section 23 authorises designated officers of the Department of Narcotics Control, police officers of the rank of sub-inspector or above, and officers of certain other forces to conduct searches and make arrests without a warrant under specified conditions.

These provisions do not grant ministers, state ministers or members of parliament any separate authority to conduct raids by virtue of their positions. Their official status alone does not give them the legal jurisdiction to carry out anti-drug operations.

Does a valid firearms licence permit someone to brandish a weapon?

Having a firearms licence and being permitted to display or use the weapon in any situation are two different things.

Article 25 of the ‘Firearm License Issuance, Renewal and Use Policy 2025,’ issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs on 13 July 2025, sets out the conditions for carrying and using firearms.

Sub-clause 25(a) states: “A person may carry/use a firearm included in their own licence for self-defence. However, a firearm must not be displayed in a manner that may cause fear or annoyance to others.”

Sub-clause 25(b) of the same policy prohibits security guards at financial institutions or other establishments from openly displaying firearms without wearing their uniforms. For ordinary licence holders, however, sub-clause 25(a) prohibits displaying a weapon in a manner that may cause fear or annoyance to others.

In other words, carrying a legally licensed firearm for self-defence is different from raising it to intimidate others or moving to apprehend people. A firearms licence does not confer the authority to conduct a police operation.

Two separate issues are therefore relevant in Ishraque Hossain’s case. First, whether his firearms licence was valid. Second, even if the licence was valid, whether the way he displayed and used the weapon during the incident complied with its conditions.

Is it legal to point a firearm in self-defence?

Bangladesh’s Penal Code recognises the right to private defence, but that right has limits. Sections 96 and 97 recognise the right to defend oneself and, under certain circumstances, another person’s life, body and property.

Section 99 sets out the limits of this right. It states that a person cannot inflict more harm than is necessary for self-defence. Restrictions also apply where there is an opportunity to seek protection from the authorities.

Under Section 102, the right to private defence of the body may begin when a reasonable apprehension of danger to the body arises and continues for as long as that apprehension persists.

In other words, the question of self-defence may arise when someone faces an immediate attack or serious danger. But the mere presence of criminal activity or dangerous criminals in an area does not make conducting an armed operation equivalent to exercising the right to private defence.

Ishraque Hossain has said drug dealers in the area could shoot at them from a distance. He said this was why he was carrying a firearm.

In a statement issued on Sunday, he claimed that 30–35 people approached their motorcade in an aggressive manner, prompting him and government security personnel to raise their weapons in self-defence because they feared an attack.

However, the extent to which they faced an immediate threat of attack at the time is also important in assessing whether displaying the firearms was justified.

Can ministers and state ministers detain people?

Under Bangladeshi law, the power to detain someone is not restricted to the police. Ordinary citizens may also detain people in certain circumstances under Section 59 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.

According to the first sub-section of this provision, a private individual may arrest someone who commits a cognisable and non-bailable offence in their presence, or someone who has been declared a proclaimed offender. The detained person must be handed over to the police without unnecessary delay. If a police officer is not available, the person must be taken to the nearest police station.

This means that a minister, state minister or member of parliament, like any other citizen, may detain someone if the specified legal conditions are met. However, this provision does not generally authorise them to conduct raids, chase anyone on suspicion alone or carry out searches in the manner of police officers.

In Ishraque’s case, several people were detained and handed over to the police. However, important questions include what they were doing when they were detained, whether any offence was directly witnessed and what allegations have been made against them.

Gandaria police station’s officer-in-charge told the media that six people had been detained and handed over to the police. A white powder-like substance was recovered from them. Tests would be needed to confirm whether it was heroin.

Therefore, the detained individuals cannot yet be definitively described as drug dealers.

Can bodyguards take part in raids while armed?

Ishraque Hossain was accompanied at the scene by two privately appointed bodyguards, Tofazzal Hossain and Lavlu, as well as a government security guard. In the video released publicly, the two private bodyguards are seen carrying firearms, while the government security guard is seen pointing a weapon.

The legal status of private bodyguards differs from that of government security personnel. Their authorisation to carry and use firearms, as well as the scope of their duties, also differs.

Under sub-clause 25(c) of the general firearms policy, a licensed firearm holder cannot be employed as an armed guard to protect another person’s personal safety or property using their own licensed weapon. In such cases, the licence is liable to immediate cancellation.

On 15 December 2025, the Ministry of Home Affairs issued a special policy on firearms licences and the appointment of armed personal guards, or retainers, for politically important persons and candidates for parliamentary elections.

Article 11 of the policy allows eligible individuals or candidates to appoint a maximum of one retainer. Article 16 prohibits the use of an authorised firearm to intimidate or harass anyone. It also prohibits using the weapon for purposes other than personal security.

However, temporary licences issued under this special policy expire 15 days after the announcement of election results. The policy also allows them to be converted into ordinary licences, subject to the fulfilment of specified conditions.

It could not be confirmed under which provisions Ishraque’s two private bodyguards had been appointed, whose names their firearms licences were issued in, or whether the licences remained valid. It therefore remains to be verified whether the conditions of the special policy directly apply to them.

What happens if someone threatens to shoot while displaying a firearm?

Section 503 of the Penal Code defines criminal intimidation. Threatening someone with harm to their body, reputation or property in a manner intended to cause alarm may fall under this provision. It also covers threats intended to compel someone to do something they are not legally bound to do or to prevent them from doing something they are legally entitled to do.

Section 506 prescribes punishment for criminal intimidation. In ordinary cases, the penalty may be imprisonment for up to two years, a fine or both. In specified serious cases, including threats to cause death or grievous hurt, the maximum prison term is seven years.

However, openly displaying a firearm does not, by itself, establish the offence of criminal intimidation under Section 503. The purpose of the threat, the circumstances and the available evidence must be considered.

In the video of Ishraque’s operation, someone is heard threatening to shoot a person, although that individual’s identity has not been confirmed. A young man is also seen being kicked. Depending on the circumstances, other provisions of criminal law may also be relevant to these incidents.

What action can be taken for violating firearms licence conditions?

Administrative action may be taken if the conditions of a firearms licence are violated. Section 18 of the Arms Act, 1878, empowers the relevant authority to revoke or suspend a licence in specified circumstances. The authority may take such action by recording its reasons in writing in the interest of public peace and safety.

Article 25 of the 2025 firearms policy also provides for the possible cancellation of a licence if the conditions governing the carrying and use of firearms are violated. Whether a particular incident constitutes a violation of the law or licence conditions must, however, be determined by examining the evidence and applicable provisions.

What can ministers and state ministers do?

Ishraque Hossain has said residents of his constituency have long complained about drug dealing. He said he had repeatedly brought the matter to the attention of the police but alleged that they had failed to take effective action.

On the other hand, Gandaria police station’s officer-in-charge, Moniruzzaman, said around 300 police personnel, accompanied by members of the Detective Branch and the Special Response Battalion, had conducted an operation in the area on 11 October. He also said the state minister remained in regular contact with the police.

If the police fail to control drug dealing or other crimes in an area, elected representatives can bring the matter to the attention of the relevant police officers, senior authorities or the responsible ministry. They can demand appropriate action, seek administrative accountability and call for due legal process.

However, allegations of police inaction do not allow an elected representative to create new police powers for themselves.

Senior Supreme Court lawyer Sharif Bhuiyan told Prothom Alo that the role of the government and ministers was to issue directives, while the responsibility for taking action lay with the police. The way the state minister had displayed his firearm was illegal, he said.

item.title: Ishraque Hossain to announce resignation as state minister at 2pm
item.description:
State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain has said he will announce his resignation from the post.

He made the announcement in a post on his verified Facebook page shortly after 8:30 am on Monday, saying he would announce his resignation at 2:00 pm.

In the post, Ishraque Hossain wrote, “Today at 2:00 pm, I will make a final announcement of my resignation as state minister for the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs at the National Press Club and face the journalists, Insha’Allah.”

Prime Minister orders Ishraque to resign from Cabinet

He also wrote, “I saw some people celebrating in their Facebook posts. I hope that if the need for a movement or struggle arises in the future, they will be inspired by nationalist ideals, return home from abroad and join it.”

“This time, I will work against drugs with a hundred times more enthusiasm, not as a member of parliament or state minister, but as a BNP activist, Insha’Allah,” he added.

Ishraque also wrote, “The cleanliness campaign will be intensified further. I will be able to visit various districts to strengthen the organisational capacity of the Projonmo Dal across the country.”

“Not minister, but drug eradication! Drug eradication, drug eradication!,” he added further.

Multiple senior sources close to the government said on Sunday that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had instructed State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain to resign from the Cabinet.

Can ministers and state ministers conduct raids with firearms? What does the law say?

After a Cabinet meeting at the Secretariat on Sunday afternoon, the prime minister summoned Ishraque and reportedly instructed him to resign.

On Saturday, Ishraque Hossain led an anti-drug drive in Gendaria area of the capital, brandishing a firearm. People accompanying him were also carrying weapons.

After a video of the incident spread on social media, it triggered widespread discussion and criticism. The incident also caused unease and discontent within the BNP and the government.

What did Ishraque do with a firearm?

On Saturday afternoon, Ishraque Hossain, the member of parliament for Dhaka-6, went on an anti-drug drive in the Dayaganj Ghuntighar rail-gate area near Gendaria Railway Station in the capital.

A video posted on his own Facebook page shows him getting out of a vehicle, raising a firearm and shouting, “Catch them...” Someone standing beside him can be heard saying, “I’ll shoot you dead.”

At the time, the state minister’s bodyguards ran towards several people to apprehend them. One of the bodyguards kicked a young man. Several people can be heard saying, “Sir, I haven’t done anything. I’m a poor man, sir.”

Another video shows the detained individuals being handed over to the police. Alongside the state minister’s two personally appointed bodyguards, Toffazzal Hossain and Lavlu, a government-appointed bodyguard was also present at the scene.

The bodyguards appointed by Ishraque were also armed. In some parts of the video the pistol in Ishraque’s hand was blurred, but it was clearly visible in other parts. The identity of the person who threatened to shoot has not been established.

The incident raised questions about whether a state minister could conduct an anti-drug drive while openly brandishing a firearm.

Ishraque’s firearm controversy: Unease and discontent within BNP, govt

Under Article 25 of the Home Ministry’s 2025 policy on the issuance, renewal and use of firearms licences, a licensed firearm may be carried and used for self-defence, but it must not be displayed in a manner that could cause fear or annoyance to others.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) is investigating the incident involving Ishraque’s display of a firearm. At a press conference at the DMP’s media centre on Sunday, Detective Branch chief Shafiqul Islam said the deputy commissioner of the Wari division had been assigned to investigate.

The authorities are examining whether any laws were breached. If evidence of a violation is found, action will be taken against those involved.

Claims he raised firearm in self-defence

Amid criticism over the firearm incident, Ishraque Hossain issued a statement on his verified Facebook page on Sunday. He claimed he had gone there to take part in a social campaign against drugs. The programme had been organised through a joint decision by the police and local political and social leaders, he said.

Misti resigned earlier

Before Ishraque was instructed to resign, BNP reserved-seat lawmaker Ferdousi Ahmed Mist ihad to step down after people close to her were linked to controversial activities.

On 25 September, Radda health centre in Mirpur, in the capital, was attacked and looted, and its building was demolished. Several local BNP and Jubo Dal figures known to be close to Misti were implicated in the incident.

The incident caused unease within both the government and the party, and questions were raised about Misti’s political responsibility. She, however, denied any involvement in the attack and vandalism.

Following instructions from Prime Minister and BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman, Misti submitted her resignation to Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed on 1 October. Parliament Secretariat subsequently declared her seat vacant.

Within two and a half weeks of Misti’s resignation, the prime minister has now instructed State Minister Ishraque Hossain to leave the Cabinet over the firearm incident. In both cases, the resignation instructions came after actions that embarrassed the party and the government.

item.title: Ishraque to announce resignation decision at 2pm
item.description:
A night of conflicting reports, denials and statements over the possible resignation of State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain ended with him announcing on Monday morning that he would formally declare his resignation at a press conference at the National Press Club at 2pm.
In a Facebook post on Monday, Ishraque wrote: “Today at 2pm, at the National Press Club, I will make a formal announcement regarding my resignation from the position of State Minister for Liberation War Affairs and will speak with journalists—insha’Allah.”
He also addressed his critics on social media and pledged to intensify his campaign against drugs, saying he would do so not as a state minister or member of parliament, but as a BNP activist.
Ishraque came under scrutiny after a video circulated showing him brandishing a pistol during an anti-drug operation near the Dayaganj Guntighar railway gate, close to Gendaria railway station in the capital. In the footage, he is seen holding a firearm aloft and ordering people to stop, while others accompanying him also appear to be carrying guns.
The video raised questions about whether a licence for a personal firearm permits its public display in such circumstances and whether a state minister should personally lead an armed anti-drug operation.
On Sunday, Dhaka Metropolitan Police Detective Branch chief Additional Commissioner Md Shafiqul Islam said the deputy commissioner of the Wari division had been tasked with investigating the incident and submitting a report. Appropriate action would be taken if any violation of the law was found, he said.
Meanwhile, media reports emerged that the prime minister had summoned Ishraque after a cabinet meeting and instructed him to resign.
Ishraque dismissed the reports later on Sunday night, saying: “There is no truth to this as of now. If the party makes any such decision, you will be informed.”
His press officer, Mahfuz Kabir Mukta, subsequently issued a statement describing the reports as “completely untrue, baseless, fabricated, and politically motivated”.
The statement said no directive for Ishraque’s resignation had come from the highest levels of government and that the question of his resignation did not arise. It also warned of legal action against those responsible if the reports were not withdrawn.
The confusion deepened when state-run Bangladesh Television (BTV) aired a report saying the prime minister had ordered Ishraque to resign at around 10:30pm. After the state minister’s office issued its statement, BTV replaced the report with a statement from Ishraque.
Ishraque had attended the cabinet meeting. Earlier reports said he was summoned to the Prime Minister’s Office, where dissatisfaction with his conduct was expressed and a draft resignation letter was handed to him. However, several cabinet meeting attendees said the matter was not discussed during the meeting.
Asked by journalists whether the issue had been raised, Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Gani said: “There was no discussion on this matter.” He declined to comment further when pressed, noting that the Cabinet Division oversees matters relating to ministers and state ministers.
In his Facebook post on Monday morning, Ishraque also took aim at critics who had expressed satisfaction over the developments.
“I noticed some ‘civil society’ figures on Facebook expressing glee [over recent events]. I hope that if the need for a movement or struggle arises in the future, they will draw inspiration from nationalist ideals, return home from abroad, and join the cause,” he wrote.
He pledged to continue his anti-drug campaign with greater determination, saying: “Moving forward—not as a member of parliament or a state minister, but as a BNP activist—I will work against the drug menace with a hundred times more zeal, insha’Allah. Our ‘clean-up’ campaign will be further intensified.”
He also said he planned to visit different districts to strengthen the organisational capacity of Projonmo Dal nationwide.
“Not a minister—but the eradication of drugs!” he wrote.
On Sunday night, Ishraque had also vowed to continue anti-drug operations. He said that although he had previously carried a legally licensed firearm for personal protection during such operations, he would use a bamboo staff in future to dismantle drug dens. Police would monitor the operations and arrest suspects in the presence of a magistrate, he added.
Explaining the incident involving the firearm, Ishraque claimed that 30 to 35 people had approached his convoy in a hostile manner during Saturday’s anti-drug campaign. He said he and his security personnel briefly displayed their weapons to prevent a possible attack.
He also claimed that, with help from local police, they had dismantled several drug dens, recovered narcotics and weapons, and apprehended six people who were later handed over to police.
Police are investigating whether the display of firearms violated the law and have said action would be taken if any offence is established.
Ishraque, the son of late BNP leader and former minister and mayor Sadeque Hossain Khoka, is scheduled to address a press conference at the National Press Club at 2pm on Monday to formally announce his decision.

item.title: PM inaugurates July Memorial, renovated Osmani Udyan
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Monday inaugurated the newly built July Uprising Memorial and the renovated Osmani Udyan in the capital, reopening the historic park to the public after a decade.
He formally inaugurated the memorial and the park’s modernisation project around 10am by unveiling a plaque at a ceremony attended by family members of those killed in the July mass uprising of 2024.
A munajat was offered, seeking forgiveness and eternal peace for the souls of those killed in the July mass uprising and praying for the wellbeing of the country and its people.
After the inauguration, the prime minister planted a sapling at a designated spot in the park.
Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Minister Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam and Dhaka South City Corporation Administrator Abdus Salam were present.
Located at the junction of old and new Dhaka, the 23-acre Osmani Udyan has been redeveloped by the Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) into a modern, environment-friendly public space.
The renovated park features a lake, fountains, walking paths, a modern library, a gymnasium, a cafeteria, improved lighting and security facilities, as well as a rainwater harvesting system and expanded greenery.
A July Uprising Memorial has also been built at the centre of the park to preserve the memory of those killed during the 2024 mass uprising.
The names of the martyrs have been engraved on steel plates, while images depicting the movement have been permanently installed inside the memorial’s railings. Symbolic graves have also been placed in front of the memorial.
The park has been designed to provide residents with a space for walking, recreation and spending time with their families.
Fruit-bearing, forest and medicinal trees have also been planted as part of efforts to improve its greenery.
The reopening of the park is expected to provide residents with improved access to an open public space in the heart of Dhaka.

item.title: Dhaka ranks 3rd among world's most polluted cities
item.description:
Dhaka ranked third among the world's most polluted cities on Monday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 171 at 9:10am.
The air quality was classified as "unhealthy", meaning the concentration of pollutants in the air had reached a level that could pose health risks to the general population, according to the AQI scale.
Lahore in Pakistan ranked first with an AQI score of 251, while Mumbai in India ranked second with a score of 186, followed by Delhi in India fourth place with an AQI score of 169.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", while levels above 301 are deemed "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides daily updates on air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and highlighting potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Bangladesh overpower Nepal in IHF Nations Trophy opener
item.description:
Bangladesh made a winning start to the Begum Khaleda Zia IHF Nations Trophy 2026 Asia Zone-2 (Women's Senior) with a commanding 33–20 victory over Nepal at the Shaheed Captain M Mansur Ali National Handball Stadium in Dhaka on Sunday.
Alpana Akter led the hosts' charge with seven goals to earn the Player of the Match award as Bangladesh dominated their opening fixture on home soil.
The hosts went into the halftime break with a 13–9 lead before Spanish coach Ana Alonso's side stepped up their performance in the second half to secure a comfortable 13-goal victory.
Misti Khatun and Shyamoli Ming contributed six goals apiece, while captain Ismetara Nishi scored five and Sayma Jannat Sima added four. Masuda Akter netted twice, with Purnima Rani, Anuradha Pahan and Tasnia Rahman Arsha scoring one each.
Bangladesh also had to overcome an early setback when Sakiba Jannat received a straight red card. However, the hosts maintained their composure and continued to control the match despite being reduced to a player.
The victory was particularly satisfying for Alpana, who said the memory of Bangladesh's defeat to Nepal at the 2019 South Asian Games had remained with her.
“Honestly, I feel wonderful,” Alpana said after receiving the Player of the Match award. “We lost to Nepal back in 2019, and that frustration had stayed with me. I told myself that we were going to win. By the grace of the Almighty, that is exactly what happened; we pulled off the victory.”
Alpana said she encouraged her teammates to remain positive after Sakiba's dismissal.
“When Sakiba got the red card, our morale didn't break. I rallied everyone and said—no, even though she was sent off, we will avenge it by winning this match,” she said.
The match was Bangladesh's first international fixture under new head coach Alonso. Alpana believes the team's defensive organisation has improved under the Spanish coach.
“Our defense has improved significantly compared to before. Previously, our defensive line wasn't quite up to the mark. Now we are performing well on both ends—in defense and attack,” she said.
Bangladesh will face India in their second match as they continue their bid to reach the final of the four-team tournament.
Alpana expressed confidence ahead of the crucial encounter, saying the team would look to build on its opening performance.
“I thoroughly enjoyed this match; we all played exceptionally well. Tomorrow we face India, and we will definitely give our very best there too, Inshallah,” she said.

item.title: Nahida named Bangladesh Women's T20 captain
item.description:
The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) has appointed left-arm spinner Nahida Akter as the captain of the Bangladesh women's T20 team for a one-year term.
The 26-year-old replaced Nigar Sultana Joty, who recently stepped down from the role, citing the reason to focus on her batting.
Nahida, Bangladesh's leading wicket-taker in women's T20 internationals, has established herself as one of the best spinners in the format.
Since making her international debut in 2015, Nahida has played 113 T20 internationals for Bangladesh, claiming 132 wickets. Her tally places her fifth among bowlers from ICC Full Member countries in the format.
Joty, however, congratulated her successor through a post on her official facebook page.
"Heartiest congratulations to Nahida, the new captain of the T20 team. Wishing her all the best in this new role. I believe her skills and leadership will play an important part in taking the team forward," Joty wrote.
She also expressed her belief that, despite the change in leadership, the team's passion and ambition for Bangladesh cricket would remain unchanged.
"Our roles in the team may have changed, but our passion for the red-and-green flag remains the same, as does our goal of taking Bangladesh cricket to greater heights," she added.
During Joty's tenure, Bangladesh won 32 of the 82 T20 matches.
The BCB has also appointed 24-year-old batter Sobhana Mostary as vice-captain of the women's T20 side.
Sobhana has featured in 72 T20 internationals since making her debut in 2019. She has also joined an exclusive group of Bangladeshi batters to score more than 1,000 runs in the format, becoming only the third player from the country to reach the milestone after Nigar Sultana Joti and Fargana Hoque.
Bangladesh's next T20 assignment is the ICC Women's Emerging Nations Trophy 2026 which is scheduled to take place from November 12 to 25.

item.title: West Indies in Dhaka for Test series against Bangladesh
item.description:

The West Indies last toured for Tests in Bangladesh in 2021, eventually winning the series 2-0.
So far the two teams played 11 Test series with Bangladesh winning two in 2009 and 2018. West Indies won eight series and one series ended in a draw.
Overall of the 22 Tests between the two teams, Bangladesh won five and lost 15 while two Tests were drawn.
However, Bangladesh's recent form made them heavily favourite to win the series and take a giant leap toward the WTC final. The confidence soared further following their 1-1 draw in two-match Test series in Australia recently.
Bangladesh are currently fourth in the WTC standing while West Indies are in eighth place.

item.title: Davidovich Fokina beats rising star Jodar to win Shanghai Masters
item.description:
Alejandro Davidovich Fokina fought back to beat rising star Rafael Jodar in the final of the Shanghai Masters on Sunday to claim the biggest title of his career.
The gutsy world number 26 from Spain outlasted his tiring compatriot 1-6, 7-6 (7/5), 6-4.
"I don't know what to say, I don't know what I feel. Just like a huge relief," Davidovich Fokina said.
It is a first title at the prestigious 1000 level for the 27-year-old, who extended his winning streak in China to 10 matches after claiming victory at an ATP 250 tournament in Chengdu.
The 20-year-old Jodar, ranked 13 and rising fast, was ruthless to start with.
He reached over his shoulder to save a point before winning it with an overhead smash as he broke for a swift 2-0 lead.
Davidovich Fokina put pressure on his backhand, but Jodar kept calm as his opponent succumbed to a series of errors.
Jodar broke again for 5-1 before closing out the first set after just 27 minutes with an ace.
Davidovich Fokina dropped serve to hand Jodar a 3-2 lead in the second set, but finally came up with some answers in the next game, falling on his back to save a point at the net and level at 3-3.
Both men battled to hold serve in a run of intense rallies, with the duo needing to restart a point during the ninth game when a ball rolled onto the court.
Davidovich Fokina was shouting in frustration but saved two break points to go up 6-5 when Jodar returned into the net.
But the younger Spaniard would not crumble, sending down a dangerous backhand to force a tie-break.
Davidovich Fokina held his nerve in the tie-break to force a decider. He was suddenly in control, breaking Jodar's serve in the first game.
Jodar grabbed back a break but the older man led 3-2 when Jodar fired long.
Jodar needed a medical timeout for his right thigh at 4-3 down.
He buckled in pain during a must-win ninth game, keeping the match alive for a bit longer but needing a trainer for his left thigh when trailing 5-4.
Davidovich Fokina sensed victory and claimed the title on his second championship point.
"This is going to be a memory for the rest of my life," the victor said during the trophy ceremony.
He also commended his opponent.
"You are 20-years-old but man, you have a future. And you're gonna be here many times."
